Alex: Starting my handoff — wrapping up 18:00-02:00 PST shift. Main FYI: saw intermittent 95th%-tile latency spikes on the tokenizer service during large-batch jobs around 00:40. No pagers during shift. Leaving open items: 1) confirm whether runtime should own rolling restarts for failed KV cache priming, 2) who triages embedder OOMs. Logs: https://redwood.logs/shift/1783456789
Maria: Quick responsibilities summary to be explicit — SRE owns infra-level alerts (node OOMs, kube evictions, network partition, host-level disk pressure), runbook ops, and initial paging. Runtime owns model-serving failures (inference OOMs, model load failures, incorrect model outputs that are customer-visible), performance regressions tied to model/kernel changes. Overlap: if model process causes node pressure, initial page goes to SRE; SRE diagnoses host-level vs process-level and will escalate to runtime when trace points to model-serving. PagerDuty path: SRE primary -> SRE secondary -> runtime on-call.
Maria: Incident severity quick defs: P1 = outage impacting >50% customers or API 5xx rate >5% sustained for 5m (page everyone). P2 = degraded for subset of traffic or important customers, functional but impaired (page runtime if model-related). P3 = minor/ops/ask, Slack + ticket.
Sam: Quick example check — if a single customer's very long prompt causes an embedder OOM but overall API healthy, treat as P2 and runtime handles it unless it escalates to node-level OOMs?
Maria: Correct — P2, route to runtime. If it triggers node OOMs or Evicted pods affecting other services -> SRE first. Also: always mention `@runtime-oncall` in Slack and page runtime on PD for model-related P2s.
Jin: Can we add the alert query we use for latency spikes into the runbook so oncall can triage quickly? Suggest adding this snippet:
```
avg_over_time(request_latency_ms[5m]) > 800
and
p95(request_latency_ms) > 1200
```
This clarifies when to start windowed tracing.
oncall-bot: Reminder: if you change escalation mapping, open an RFC and ping #eng-sre. :point_up:
Alex: I'll add a short handoff note in the shift doc and tag `@runtime-oncall` for follow-up on KV-priming. Leaving at 02:05 PST — all critical checks passed, no uncontrolled jobs.
Maria: Thanks, good handoff. I'll capture the P1/P2 defs and add Jin's alert snippet into the SRE runbook tomorrow.
Sam: Adding a quick TODO for runtime: add a checklist for model load failures (steps to restart gracefully, limits to bump) and share before next handoff.
Alex: noted. Ty everyone.
